title: Elastic Session Crediting and Migration Playbook
author: Gina Morales
content:
Overview

This playbook defines the Elastic Session Crediting (ESC) model and the recommended migration strategy for customers moving from flat token-based billing to session-aware, elastic credits. The ESC model is designed to:

- Stabilize tenant economics for conversational workloads with bursty traffic patterns.
- Preserve fidelity guarantees (per-route SLOs) while enabling automated credit top-ups and graceful degradation.
- Reduce billing surprises at month-end by aligning session semantics with capacity reservations and transient credits.

Scope

Applies to: Hosted API customers, Dedicated tenants, and Private deployments that opt into ESC.
Exclusions: Pure embedding-only customers (unless they enable conversational sessions) and legacy accounts on fixed-token plans that do not opt into migration.

Goals and success metrics

Primary goals:
1) Reduce monthly overage disputes by 60% for customers who migrate to ESC.
2) Reduce average cost-per-interaction for 95th percentile session lengths by 20% versus flat per-token pricing (measured in a 30-day A/B cohort).
3) Maintain per-route latency SLOs (p99 < target) and fidelity error budgets at parity with current plans.

Key metrics to track:
- Migration adoption rate (week-over-week %)
- Monthly overage dispute volume and escalations
- Effective cost-per-session and cost-per-token (median and 95th pct)
- SLO compliance delta before/after migration (latency/p99, error-rate)
- Customer satisfaction (NPS change for migrated cohorts)

Elastic Session Crediting model: concepts

- Session Unit (SU): A lightweight accounting primitive representing an active conversational session. SUs are consumed over time according to the session’s interaction pattern and configured fidelity bucket.
- Base SU allocation: A monthly baseline assigned per-customer (or per-tenant) packaged with reserved capacity (Dedicated) or purchased as a warm subscription (Hosted).
- Elastic Top-up Credits (ETC): On-demand credits consumed when session usage exceeds base SU allocation; configured with soft limits and auto-topup policies.
- Fidelity Buckets: Classes that map model variants and quantization profiles to SU consumption multipliers (e.g., low: 0.6x, medium: 1x, high: 1.75x).
- Graceful Degradation Policy (GDP): Ordered fallback rules when SU supply is insufficient (e.g., degrade fidelity -> route to cheaper variant -> enqueue with retry).

Billing formula (simplified)

Monthly charge = Reserved package fee + SU overage * SU unit price + (ETC consumed * ETC unit price) - any migration credits/discounts

Where SU overage = max(0, total SUs consumed - base SU allocation). Default SU unit price is derived from historical per-token economics and adjusted by fidelity multiplier.

Example pricing table (illustrative)

| Tier | Base SUs / month | SU price | ETC price | Fidelity multiplier (med) | Notes |
|------|------------------:|---------:|----------:|-------------------------:|-------|
| Starter | 10,000 | $0.0015 | $0.0020 | 1.0 | Self-serve SMBs |
| Growth  | 250,000 | $0.0011 | $0.0016 | 1.0 | PLG growth accounts |
| Enterprise | 5,000,000 | $0.0008 | $0.0012 | 1.0 | SLA-backed |

Design constraints and guardrails

- Must integrate with existing usage pipeline (telemetry ingestion, cost attribution, billing reconciliation) without material latency impact.
- Synchronous API surface must remain unchanged for developer ergonomics; crediting occurs server-side.
- GDPR/CCPA: SU and ETC records must respect data residency; aggregates only in billing exports unless customer agreement allows itemized session logs.
- Backwards compatibility: Customers who do not opt-in continue on token billing with a translatable exchange rate for migration credits.

Telemetry and observability requirements

1) Per-tenant session-level telemetry: session_id, tenant_id, start_ts, end_ts, SU_consumed, fidelity_bucket, topup_events. (Exported as line-delimited JSON to internal telemetry stream.)
2) Per-route dashboards: SU consumption heatmaps, ETC burn rate, topup latency, GDP triggers.
3) Billing reconciliation hooks: daily aggregated SU tallies and topup records pushed to billing queue.
4) Alerting: ETC burn rate > 80% of purchased ETC across 24h for three consecutive days -> Sales Ops alert.

Migration playbook (customer-facing steps)

Phase 0 — Pre-migration (Product/CS/Support)
- Identify candidate accounts: high volatility session traffic or frequent monthly overages. Use query: avg_monthly_overage > 10% OR monthly_escapes > 3.
- Run simulation: use last 90 days of telemetry to simulate ESC SU consumption and estimated monthly bill. Provide a 2-week beta discount for adoption.
- Prepare customer-specific migration summary: expected monthly cost delta, recommended fidelity limits, and fallback preferences.

Phase 1 — Opt-in and onboarding (0–7 days)
1. Sales/CS sends migration offer via the Console (automated workflow).
2. Customer accepts and selects base SU package + topup policy (manual/auto).
3. System runs dry-run for seven days with no billing impact and shows live estimator in Console.
4. Address questions: support playbook includes an FAQ, sample invoices, and troubleshooting runbook.

Phase 2 — Cutover (day 8–30)
- Soft cutover: After acceptance, traffic is routed under ESC accounting but token billing remains available as a reconciliation snapshot.
- Week 1: Monitor key telemetry (SU burn, latency SLOs, ETC triggers).
- Automated rollback: If GDP triggers exceed thresholds (see rollback criteria below), revert billing to token model for 48h and open expedited customer review.

Phase 3 — Post-migration (30–90 days)
- Evaluate billing delta, SLO compliance, and NPS feedback.
- If customer opts for Dedicated, transfer base SU allocation into reserved capacity contract and update SLA mapping.
- Offer a one-time migration credit if actual charges exceed the simulation by > 25% in first full month.

Rollback criteria (automatic)

Trigger an automated rollback to token billing if any of the following occur within the first 14 days post-cutover:
1) p99 latency breach > 2x target for > 30 minutes caused by crediting logic;
2) ETC topup failure rate > 5% for > 1 hour;
3) Unexpected billing delta > 40% vs dry-run estimate OR billing disputes initiated by the customer.

Operational runbook snippets

- Checkpoint: If a customer reports unexpected charges: 1) validate session_id and SU consumption ledger via billing reconciliation API; 2) run the dry-run simulator for their last 90 days; 3) escalate to Billing Ops for provisional credit if discrepancy found.
- Topup failure troubleshooting: verify KMS signing keys for charge authorization, check payment method status, and inspect topup queue for backpressure.

Rollout timeline and milestones (Q2–Q4 2029)

- Q2 2029: Internal alpha (billing pipeline integration and Console estimator).
- Q3 2029: Pilot with 10 customers (Growth and Enterprise) + telemetry validation.
- Q4 2029: General availability for Hosted and Dedicated; Private GA gating on admin migration controls.

Open questions and decisions pending

- Final SU unit price bands for Starter and Growth tiers (Finance modeling complete by 2029-05-15).
- Console UX for multi-tenant accounts with per-team base SU allocations.
- Whether to allow itemized session logs in billing exports by default or opt-in only for Enterprise.

Appendices

A. Console estimator CLI example

redwood estimate-esc --tenant t_123 --range 2029-01-01:2029-03-31 --simulate 
# Output: estimated_monthly_su: 348,200; est_cost: $382.12; recommended_tier: Growth

B. Example GDP chain (default)
1. Degrade fidelity (high -> medium -> low)
2. Route to cheaper model variant with KV eviction disabled
3. If still under-provisioned, return a 429 with structured retry-after and telemetry tag 'ESC_GDP'

C. Migration FAQs (selected)
- Q: Will session credits expire? A: Base SUs are monthly and do not carry over. Purchased ETC may be purchased as one-off bundles (30/90/365 day expiry options).
- Q: How do we track SU consumption? A: Per-session aggregates are visible in the Console and exported daily to the billing S3 bucket in CSV form.

For questions, feedback, or to request an early pilot, contact: product@redwood.ai or open a ticket referencing ESC-PLAYBOOK-2029.
